A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, renamed from β-calibration to QA-calibration. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 and Tables 2, 6, and 7 report original calibration and selective-QA experiments across five datasets.

after.justification: The original experiments are retained, with additional grouping-choice experiments, partition examples, and calibration diagnostics in Appendices E–H.

M1.justification: The binning and hierarchical-scaling algorithms remain unchanged under their new names. Appendix F adds concrete variants of the grouping component using XLNet embeddings and k-means alongside DistilBERT and kd-trees, a limited extension within the existing β framework.

E1.justification: Both versions use TriviaQA, SciQ, BigBench, OpenBookQA, and MMLU for calibration and selective QA. The additional analyses reuse OpenBookQA without introducing another dataset, task, domain, or input scenario.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain uncalibrated elicitation (None), UMD histogram binning (B), Platt scaling (S), and scaling-binning (S-B). Table 9 and Figures 3–4 reuse these comparators. BB, S-BB, and HS-BB are renamed QAB, S-QAB, and HS-QAB.

E3.justification: The original 20:60:10:10 split remains. New experiments cross embedding and partitioner choices, tune k-means centroid counts using AUAC, and assess partition-wise ECE with depth-two trees. AUAC prose also changes from inclusive to strict confidence thresholds, although the adjacent selection rule remains inclusive; an implementation change or rerun is not established.

E4.justification: Appendices E–H substantially expand the diagnostics beyond the original benchmark comparisons: sampled partition contents (Table 8), embedding/partitioner sensitivity (Table 9), confidence transformations (Figure 3), and partition-wise reliability (Figure 4). These examine grouping coherence, dependence on β choices, and calibration within individual groups.

E5.justification: Appendix B.1 in both versions specifies eight random splits using different seeds to form confidence intervals. Table 9 extends the existing uncertainty-reporting practice; no changed run count, interval-estimation procedure, or significance test is reported.

E6.justification: All 140 original benchmark rows match after renaming and relocation. Supplementary OpenBookQA results are added: Table 9 reports S-QAB with XLNet/k-means at CE 0.235 ± 0.010 and AUAC 0.350 ± 0.018, while Figure 4 shows QAB attaining the lowest ECE in all four displayed partitions. These are additional findings, not improvements to retained scores.

T1.justification: Appendix D adds Definition D.1, generalizing maximum calibration error by maximizing over QA partitions and confidence values. V1 only discusses standard MCE. The existing calibration definitions, distribution-free bounds, and proofs otherwise remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain group-conditional calibration, two posthoc calibration schemes, distribution-free guarantees, and improved calibration/selective QA. The abstract newly summarizes guarantees and validation already claimed in v1's introduction. The stated 10–40% calibration and up-to-30% selective-answering improvements are retained.

C2.justification: New discussion interprets partition-specific score variation as greater sharpness, identifies topic-based versus question-form groupings in Table 8, and notes that reliability analysis becomes unwieldy with many partitions. The original limitations concerning partition granularity and a fixed β output space remain.

D1.justification: The new analyses document pretrained XLNet [CLS] embeddings, AUAC-based centroid selection, depth-seven trees for sampled partition examples, and depth-two trees for reliability plots. Existing prompt templates, querying guidance, and the 3090Ti GPU/64 GB RAM disclosure are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds Gneiting et al. (2007) for sharpness and Yang et al. (2019) for XLNet. It removes the random-projection-tree future-work suggestion and its Dasgupta and Freund (2008) citation. The main positioning against prior calibration research remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The title and method terminology change from β-calibration/BB to QA-calibration/QAB, and βhist becomes βbin. There are localized prose revisions, an expanded abstract, and acknowledgements. The main section order and most existing explanations remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adopts ICLR typography and extensively rearranges displays. BigBench rows move from Table 2 to Table 7, Table 3 moves ahead of Appendix A, and Figure 2 receives a side caption. Tables 8–9 and Figures 3–4 add substantial new visual material, including four reliability panels.

improvement.justification: The added grouping-choice experiments, partition examples, and reliability diagnostics provide useful support for mechanisms that v1 mainly motivated conceptually or assessed through aggregate results. Original benchmark results and guarantees are preserved. The gain is limited because the new empirical checks focus on OpenBookQA/Mistral, and v2 introduces an ambiguity in AUAC threshold wording.
